scenarios: a hook rewrites change.apply onto rewritten.txt: the rewrite runs, its change record and the result's arguments_hash are the rewrite's
under a policy denying fs.write the rewritten call is denied by the kernel
a rewrite onto .env is refused; a schema-breaking rewrite is HOOK_REWRITE_INVALID
audit: DOCUMENTED-ONLY before: no interception existed; the pipeline's monotonic verdict (REQ-EV-0239) did.
proof: Real Core: an intercepting hook's rewrite goes back through schema, custody check and the Capability Kernel, which decides last.
negative_proof: No rewrite clears a kernel deny or reaches a protected path.

ci.note: every job green on macOS, Linux and Windows on the rebased head (after IMP-EV-0029 landed); one change carries IMP-EV-0042, 0139 and 0240

limitations: Handlers run as host processes with a scrubbed environment (not sandboxed further, like MCP stdio servers); payloads are summaries; only tool arguments can be rewritten; no signature or marketplace trust on extensions in this change (IMP-EV-0225).
